subject: current_onboarding_process
statement: Today HR collects onboarding data in a Word document and an Excel file, then types everything into the portals by hand. Last month two new hires took a full afternoon.

anchors.quote: I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand.
Last month I spent a full afternoon on two new hires.

subject: hiring_volume
statement: Muster AG hires around twenty people a year, more in summer. It has about 150 employees, mostly in Zurich.

anchors.quote: Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.

subject: source_tax_pain
statement: Source tax is HR's biggest time sink. Because HR does not know up front who must answer the source tax questions, it sends the whole questionnaire to everybody, which annoys Swiss employees.

anchors.quote: Source tax, without any doubt.
So I send the whole questionnaire to everybody, and the Swiss people get annoyed, and they call me.

subject: source_tax_questions
statement: Source tax questions should only be asked of employees who are subject to source tax, not of everybody.

anchors.quote: Because I never know up front who has to answer those questions.
So who actually needs to answer them?

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: First version: all non-Swiss employees (anyone without a Swiss passport) are subject to source tax.

anchors.quote: All the non-Swiss employees. Simple as that. If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.

subject: source_tax_calculator
statement: The source tax questionnaire is the canton of Zurich's online tariff calculator, which outputs the tariff code. HR uses the Zurich calculator for everybody and acknowledges that this is not exactly how it works. Leo agreed to keep it that way for now.

anchors.quote: I use the Zurich calculator on the canton's website. The one that gives you the tariff code.
For everybody I use Zurich, by the way. I know it's not exactly how it works, but that's what we do for now.
Understood. We'll keep that for now.

subject: source_tax_calculator
statement: Today HR clicks through the Zurich calculator manually using the employee's answers.

anchors.quote: I sit with the answers and click through it.

subject: home_address
statement: HR needs the employee's home address because HR posts many documents to employees.

anchors.quote: Yes, I need the address, obviously.
We post a lot of documents to people, so it has to be complete.

subject: home_address
statement: The address must be complete: street, house number, postcode, town and country.

anchors.quote: The full address. Street, number, postcode, town, country.

subject: home_address
statement: Nothing beyond a normal postal address is needed, the way you would write it on an envelope.

anchors.quote: No, no. Just a normal address, the way you would write it on an envelope.

subject: employee_name
statement: HR needs the employee's name. Leo asked about 'Name, address' and Anna answered 'Yes', but she only elaborated on the address.

anchors.quote: What about the basics? Name, address, that kind of thing?
Yes, I need the address, obviously.

subject: photo
statement: HR would like the form to ask for a photo for employee badges. Today reception takes poor phone pictures.

anchors.quote: Oh, that would be so nice, actually. For the badges.
Could the form ask for a photo?

subject: photo
statement: The photo is out of scope for now because security is changing the badge system next year. It may be revisited next year.

anchors.quote: Let's not do that now. Forget the photo for the moment, we'll talk about it next year.
Okay, no photo.

subject: pension_fund
statement: Muster AG's pension fund is Pensionskasse Muster, which has an old portal. Anna will send screenshots of it.

anchors.quote: We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old.
I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call

subject: first_working_day
statement: The pension fund needs the employee's first working day. Anna calls it the number one item.

anchors.quote: I need their first working day. That's the number one thing

subject: first_working_day
statement: The employee should confirm the first working day, because it changes often (for example, when people negotiate an earlier exit with their old employer).

anchors.quote: I ask them to confirm it, because it moves more often than you'd think.
People negotiate with their old employer, they get out a week earlier.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: First version: pension fund insurance starts on the first day of the month after the first working day (for example, first working day 15.03 gives insurance start 01.04).

anchors.quote: because insurance starts on the first of the following month. So for her that was the first of April

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: Exception: if the first working day is the first day of a month, insurance starts on that same day.

anchors.quote: Unless somebody starts exactly on the first, of course, then it's just that day.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: Consolidated rule: the insurance start date is derived from the first working day. If the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day. Otherwise it starts on the 1st of the following month.

anchors.quote: because insurance starts on the first of the following month.
Unless somebody starts exactly on the first, of course, then it's just that day.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: When the first working day changes, the insurance start date given to the pension fund must be re-derived and updated. A missed update (Julia) caused a wrong date at the fund, an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing.

anchors.quote: She moved her first working day to the 15th of March, and I didn't update it.
I got a very unfriendly letter.
It took weeks to fix.

subject: civil_status
statement: The pension fund asks for the employee's civil status.

anchors.quote: Yes, the civil status. They ask for that.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: If the employee is married, the pension fund wants the spouse's date of birth.

anchors.quote: And if someone is married, they want the date of birth of the husband or wife.

subject: civil_status
statement: Anna is unsure of the civil status options. From memory she named Single, Married, Divorced and ('I think') Widowed, and said the screenshots will show the actual list.

anchors.quote: I'd have to look. You'll see it in the screenshots. Single, married, divorced, I think widowed.

subject: civil_status
statement: At least one current employee (Daniel, finance) is in a registered partnership, so this case occurs.

anchors.quote: we do have one colleague in a registered partnership. Daniel, in finance.

subject: civil_status
statement: Anna does not know how the pension fund's screen handles a registered partnership, or whether the fund wants the partner's details (for example, date of birth).

anchors.quote: I honestly don't know what the fund's screen does in that case, or if they want the partner's details too.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Correction: non-Swiss employees with a C permit are not subject to source tax. They are treated like Swiss people (example: Maria, Portuguese, C permit).

anchors.quote: No, that's actually not right.
So, not the people with a C permit. They're treated like Swiss people for this.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Leo summarised the rule as 'non-Swiss, but not with a C permit'. Anna only answered 'I think so' (hedged), and later added more conditions.

anchors.quote: Okay, so non-Swiss, but not with a C permit. Is that everything?
I think so.

subject: nationality
statement: The employee's nationality is needed to decide whether they are subject to source tax.

anchors.quote: If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.

subject: permit_type
statement: The permit type of non-Swiss employees is needed to decide source tax liability (a C permit exempts them). The permit type is only relevant for non-Swiss employees.

anchors.quote: So, not the people with a C permit.

subject: payroll_numbers
statement: Anna offered to get numbers from the payroll person on how long the source tax work takes.

anchors.quote: Do you want some numbers on how long this takes? I could get that for you from our payroll person.

subject: it_equipment
statement: IT equipment (laptops) is out of scope. IT has its own process.

anchors.quote: IT does laptops, they have their own process, keep them out of this, please.

subject: permit_reminder
statement: HR would love the form to remind employees to bring their permit on the first day, because half of them forget. Leo deferred the wording, so this is not decided.

anchors.quote: What I would love is if the form could remind people to bring their permit. Half of them forget.
We can look at the wording later.

subject: spouse_employment
statement: For married employees, the source tax calculator asks whether the spouse works.

anchors.quote: It changes the questions in the calculator, yes. Whether the husband or wife works.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: An employee married to a Swiss person, or to someone with a C permit, is not subject to source tax if that spouse lives 'here'. Example: Tomás, Brazilian with a B permit, has a Swiss wife and they live in Winterthur, so he has no source tax.

anchors.quote: If you're married to someone Swiss, or to someone with a C permit, and that person lives here, then you don't do source tax either.
Tomás in logistics, for example. Brazilian, B permit, but his wife is Swiss, and they live in Winterthur. So no source tax for him.

subject: spouse_check
statement: Today HR checks the spouse exemption by hand and asks for the spouse details by email, which takes forever.

anchors.quote: I always have to check that one by hand.
I ask them by email, and it takes forever.

subject: spouse_nationality
statement: For source tax, HR needs the spouse's nationality.

anchors.quote: So you need to know about the spouse as well.
Yes. Their nationality, their permit if they have one, and that they live here.

subject: spouse_permit_type
statement: For source tax, HR needs the spouse's permit, if the spouse has one.

anchors.quote: their permit if they have one

subject: spouse_residence_country
statement: For source tax, HR needs to know whether the spouse lives 'here'.

anchors.quote: and that they live here.

subject: spouse_source_tax_questions
statement: The spouse's nationality, permit and residence only matter for source tax when the employee is married. They are presumably only needed when the employee would otherwise be subject to source tax (non-Swiss, no C permit, living in Switzerland).

anchors.quote: it also changes who has to do it at all.
then you don't do source tax either.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Employees who work here but live abroad (examples: Konstanz in Germany, Liechtenstein) are always subject to source tax, regardless of nationality. Even a Swiss citizen living abroad (Stefan) is subject.

anchors.quote: Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here.
And there it doesn't matter what passport you have, by the way. Stefan is actually Swiss, and he still has it.
So someone living abroad and working here always does it?
Yes.

subject: cross_border_employees
statement: A few employees live across the border, for example Stefan in Konstanz (Germany) and a warehouse employee in Liechtenstein.

anchors.quote: We have a few who live across the border. Stefan lives in Konstanz, and there's a woman in the warehouse who lives in Liechtenstein.

subject: address_country
statement: The employee's country of residence (the country of the home address) is needed to decide source tax liability for cross-border employees.

anchors.quote: Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here.

subject: cross_border_source_tax_questions
statement: For employees living abroad, the calculator asks more questions, and Germany has its own forms. Anna cannot remember what they are called. Leo deferred to the calculator, so the exact questions are unresolved in this transcript.

anchors.quote: And with them the calculator gets much more complicated, there are more questions. Germany has its own forms, I can never remember what they're called.
Okay, that's fine, the calculator will tell us.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Consolidated final rule. An employee who lives abroad (outside Switzerland) is subject to source tax regardless of nationality. An employee who lives in Switzerland is subject only if they are non-Swiss without a C permit and are not married to a Swiss national or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland. Note: Anna said 'here', which is read as Switzerland. Her 'I think' hedges remain.

anchors.quote: If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.
So, not the people with a C permit. They're treated like Swiss people for this.
If you're married to someone Swiss, or to someone with a C permit, and that person lives here, then you don't do source tax either.
Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here.
Yes.

subject: project_timing
statement: Anna asked when the product will be available. Leo will answer this week, after reviewing the pension fund screenshots.

anchors.quote: Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
